sources.entry: akou - Records calls and meetings, transcribes them on-device with speaker labels, and lets Claude Code or Codex question a call over MCP.

summary.one_liner: akou is a macOS desktop app that records your calls locally, transcribes them on-device with speaker labels, and lets your terminal agent (Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client) question a call while it runs.
summary.what_it_does: akou records the microphone and call audio on separate channels without joining the meeting as a bot and without a virtual audio driver. It shows a live transcript during the call and runs a more accurate pass with speaker labels on the Mac afterward. A timestamped notepad lets you write notes during the call. Ask answers questions about the call using Claude Code or Codex, a local model, or your own API key, and falls back to searching the call when no provider is set. Your terminal agent can start, follow, question and annotate calls over a local API or MCP, and finished calls can be handed off as Markdown, an event log and audio via an export folder, hooks, a signed webhook, or the API. The same core also runs as a self-hosted transcription server in Docker, with file jobs, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and Wyoming and Bazarr /asr endpoints.
use_cases: record and transcribe a meeting locally on a Mac
let Claude Code or Codex follow a live call
ask questions about a call while it is running
export meeting notes to a markdown vault or repository
dictate text into any app with a hotkey
run a self-hosted transcription server in Docker
get speaker-labelled transcripts after a call
how_to_run: akou skill install (after installing the command line from the akou menu, to let Claude Code or Codex follow calls)
notable: Records mic and call audio on separate channels with no bot in the meeting and no virtual audio driver
Terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex, or MCP clients) can follow and question a call live
Everything stays on your machine with no account and no cloud, per the README
Same core runs as a self-hosted Docker transcription server with OpenAI-compatible and Wyoming endpoints
Push-to-hold dictation types into any app; learns corrected words only with your confirmation
caveats: The desktop app runs only on macOS with Apple silicon; Windows and Linux get only the command-line tool, which cannot record
First launch downloads speech models of about 3.0 GB
Ask needs Claude Code, Codex, a local model, or your own API key to answer questions; otherwise it only searches the call
